issue.body:
## I'm submitting a... 

[ ] Regression (a behavior that used to work and stopped working in a new release)
[ ] Bug report  
[x] Feature request
[ ] Documentation issue or request
[ ] Support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
Supersedes #14620 with more concrete summary and design. ## Current behavior It's currently not possible to wrap an existing provider in the same injector, which causing: #### Class inheritance problems + #19181, #21697, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/22011#discussion_r166260795, ... (`class extends ErrorHandler`) + #18976 (`class extends Location`) *In Angular, the constructor is not consider public API due to the DI system, so extending class would be problematic and may require lots of boilerplate (declare deps again).* #### Customize existing service problems + #22024 (`RendererFactory2`) + #16184 (`DefaultRouteReuseStrategy`) *The declared class may not be same to the provided one, the latter may not be exposed to user.* #### Strategy pattern design problems + #3929 (`Renderer`) + #11309, #18554 (`IterableDiffers`) + #18155, #19852 (`HttpInterceptor`) *Extends behavior of some poor-designed services.* ## Expected behavior #### API Design The term `decorator` is not fit to this any more (due to other meanings), currently choose `intercept` for similar usage to `HttpInterceptor`. (still open to bikeshed) An optional `intercept` property like `multi` applies to all kinds of providers: ```typescript @Injectable() class CustomErrorHandler implements ErrorHandler { constructor(private handler: ErrorHandler) {} handleError(error: any) { // custom error collecting or reporting this.handler.handleError(error) } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler, intercept: true } ] }) class AppModule { } ``` #### Semantics Ref: [AngularJS Decorator API](https://docs.angularjs.org/guide/decorators). By setting `intercept: true`, it would allowed to inject (previous instance of) the token it providers, so it helps reusing existing logic (no need to rewrite) without modifying the consumer part (in same token). So only combining with `useClass` or `useFactory` makes sense. `{ provide: TOKEN, useExisting: TOKEN, intercept: true }` would not be allowed. `{ provide: TOKEN, useValue: VALUE, intercept: true }` is technically valid but meaningless, could cause either warning or error. Edge case: for `multi: true` provider, interceptor should transform the instances array, namely getting the existing array and returning a new array. `{ provide: TOKEN, useClass: CLASS, multi: true, intercept: true }` would not be allowed, as it cannot return an array. Inconsistent `multi` value between concrete provider and interceptor in same injector would not be allowed. #### Scoping Any interceptor would belong to a specific `Injector` thus supporting inheritance. For example: ```typescript @Component({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useFactory: func2, deps: [ErrorHandler], intercept: true }, ] }) class MyComponent { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func2(func1(/*original*/ErrorHandler)) } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useFactory: func1, deps: [ErrorHandler], intercept: true }, ] }) class MyModule { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func1(/*original*/ErrorHandler) } } ``` Providing the normal instance won't be affected by interceptor in parent `Injector`. For example: ```typescript @Component({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler }, ] }) class MyComponent { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> CustomErrorHandler } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useFactory: func1, deps: [ErrorHandler], intercept: true }, ] }) class MyModule { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func1(/*original*/ErrorHandler) } } ``` Should intercepting `multi: true` providers at each level. For example: (Without #18894) ```typescript @Component({ providers: [ { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler3, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler4, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useFactory: func2, deps: [ErrorHandler], multi: true, intercept: true }, ] }) class MyComponent { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func2([errorHandler3, errorHandler4]) } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler1, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler2, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useFactory: func1, deps: [ErrorHandler], multi: true, intercept: true }, ] }) class MyModule { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func1([errorHandler1, errorHandler2]) } } ``` (With #18894) ```typescript @Component({ providers: [ { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler3, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler4, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useFactory: func2, deps: [ErrorHandler], multi: true, intercept: true }, ] }) class MyComponent { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func2([...func1([errorHandler1, errorHandler2]), errorHandler3, errorHandler4]) } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler1, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useValue: errorHandler2, multi: true }, { provide: ERROR_HANDLERS, useFactory: func1, deps: [ErrorHandler], multi: true, intercept: true }, ] }) class MyModule { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> func1([errorHandler1, errorHandler2]) } } ``` #### Ordering All interceptors are considered `multi` provider and applied last (local to `Injector`). For example: ```typescript @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler1 }, { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler2, intercept: true }, { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler3 }, { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler4, intercept: true }, ] }) class AppModule { constructor(handler: ErrorHandler) { // handler -> new CustomErrorHandler4(new CustomErrorHandler2(new CustomErrorHandler3(/* ... */))) } } ``` #### Examples Reduce class inheritance: ```typescript @Injectable() class CustomErrorHandler implements ErrorHandler { constructor(private handler: ErrorHandler) {} handleError(error: any) { // custom error collecting or reporting this.handler.handleError(error) } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: ErrorHandler, useClass: CustomErrorHandler, intercept: true } ] }) class AppModule { } ``` Protect private APIs: ```typescript @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: RendererFactory2, useClass: CustomRendererFactory2, intercept: true } ] }) class AppModule { } ``` Applying new strategy: Actually this is not the best way to solve that problem, exposing `DifferFactory` as a multi provider would be better, but this could work without changing existing APIs. ```typescript @Injectable() class CustomIterableDiffers implements IterableDiffers { constructor(private differs: IterableDiffers) {} get factories(): IterableDifferFactory[] { return this.differs.factories } find(iterable: any): IterableDifferFactory { if (iterable[SOME_SPECIAL_TOKEN]) { return superPerformantDifferFactory } return this.differs.find(iterable) } } @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: IterableDiffers, useClass: CustomIterableDiffers, intercept: true } ] }) class AppModule { } ``` Custom control over existing strategy: ```typescript const disabledInterceptors = new WeakMap>>() @NgModule({ providers: [ { provide: HTTP_INTERCEPTORS, useFactory: enableFiltering, multi: true, intercept: true }, InterceptorControlService, ] }) class AppModule { } function enableFiltering(interceptors: HttpInterceptor) { return interceptors.map(interceptor => ({ intercept(req: HttpRequest, next: HttpHandler): Observable> { if (disabledInterceptors.has(req) && disabledInterceptors.get(req).has(interceptor.constructor)) { return next.handle(req) } return next.handle(interceptor.intercept(req, next)) } })) } @Injectable() class InterceptorControlService { disable(request: HttpRequest, interceptorType: Type) { if (!disabledInterceptors.has(request)) { disabledInterceptors.set(request, new Set()) } disabledInterceptors.get(request).add(interceptorType) } } @Component({ /*...*/ }) class MyComponent { constructor(http: HttpClient, interceptorControl: InterceptorControlService) { const request = http.post(/*...*/) interceptorControl.disable(request, SomeCustomInterceptor) request.subscribe(/*...*/) } } ``` #### Implementation Each `Injector` should hold a internal slot of interceptors, a naive logical demo could be: ```typescript // Didn't consider `multi: true` yet class Injector_ { private interceptedInjectables = new Map() private providerInterceptors = new Map() hasInterceptors(token: any) { return this.providerInterceptors.has(token) || (!this.hasLocalProvider(token) && this.parent.hasInterceptors(token)) } getInterceptors(token: any) { return [...(this.hasLocalProvider(token) ? [] : this.parent.getInterceptors(token)), this.providerInterceptors.get(token)] } get(token: any) { if (this.interceptedInjectables.has(token)) { return this.interceptedInjectables.get(token) } if (this.hasInterceptors(token)) { const raw = getRawProviderSomehow(token) const interceptors = this.getInterceptors(token) const res = interceptors.reduce( (previousInstance, currentProvider) => instantiateSomehow(currentProvider, previousInstance), raw) this.interceptedInjectables.set(token, res) return res } // original logic } } ``` **For performance consideration (static ones):** + To get rid of mapping, the `interceptors` slot should be directly added to `providerDef` instance via `Compiler`; + If an injector has only **provider interceptor** but not **concrete provider**, use a `providerDef` with value of special symbol `NO_VALUE` to ship `interceptors`; **Tree-shakable consideration (static ones):** Extend `@Inject()` decorator to accept an additional optional parameter: ```typescript @Component({ /*...*/ }) class MyComponent { constructor( @Inject(HttpClient, logRequest) http: HttpClient ) {} } // makeParamDecorator('Inject', (token: any, ...interceptors: any[]) => ({token, interceptors})) ``` Or introduce a new decorator: ```typescript @Component({ /*...*/ }) class MyComponent { constructor( @Intercept(logRequest) http: HttpClient ) {} } // makeParamDecorator('Intercept', (...interceptors: any[]) => ({interceptors})) ``` Child injectors should not be affected in this way. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions Could go to #14620 for repro of current behavior. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? ~~Provide a demo of how to raise concrete feature request~~ Make the DI mechanism more powerful and useful. ## Environment

## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->

Issue Number: #11309, #18554

The static method `IterableDiffers.extend()` cannot be used in application injector and isn't AOT compatible.

## What is the new behavior?

Deprecate `IterableDiffers.extend()`, instead make `IterableDiffers.create()` to add `DefaultIterableDifferFactory` in the end.

For extending at application-level, just use `IterableDiffers.create()` method:

```typescript
@NgModule({
  providers: [
    { provide: IterableDiffers, useValue: IterableDiffers.create([customDifferFactory]) }
  ]
})
class AppModule {}
```

For extending at directive-level, provide a factory function:

```typescript
export function extendIterableDiffers(parent: IterableDiffers): IterableDiffers {
  return IterableDiffers.create([customDifferFactory], parent)
}

@Component({
  providers: [
    { provide: IterableDiffers, useFactory: extendIterableDiffers, deps: [[new SkipSelf(), IterableDiffers]] }
  ]
})
class AppComponent {}
```


## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?
```
[ ] Yes
[x] No
```

`DefaultIterableDifferFactory` is added in the end, which will always be overriden by custom `IterableDifferFactory`s.

issue.body:
Differs tries to inject parent differ in order to support extending.
This does not work in the 'root' injector as the provider overrides the
default injector. The fix is to just assume standard set of providers
and extend those instead.

PR Close #25015
Issue close #11309 `Can't extend IterableDiffers`
Issue close #18554 `IterableDiffers.extend is not AOT compatible` (This is fixed because we no longer have an arrow function in the  factory but a proper function which can be imported.)
